task.title: Replace the web handler's positional capability list with an options struct
task.description:
webui.newHandler reached twelve positional parameters across two consecutive stories: ten when the history view added TaskHistoryReader, twelve when the optimistic web queue added sync state reporting and mode setting. Replace the positional list with an options struct.

Blast radius measured 2026-08-06 at commit c453596. Production call sites: exactly one, internal/cli/run.go:819-863. Tests reference the constructors about 79 times. The constructor is self-documenting about the problem at internal/webui/handler.go:209-215.

The genuinely dangerous pairs are delete and restore (handler.go:34-36) and depend and free (handler.go:38-40): identical signatures, so a mis-ordering compiles and silently inverts the semantics.

This is not theoretical. Swapping the delete and restore literals in runServe compiles and leaves go test ./... -count=1 fully green while board deletion is broken, because DELETE /api/tasks/{id}, POST /api/tasks/{id}/restore, and GET /api/tasks/{id}/history have no test through the real runServe wiring. They are covered only at handler level with injected fakes, which cannot catch a wiring swap by construction.

So the refactor and the missing serve-level tests are two halves of one fix, and the tests are the half that actually closes the hole: an options struct makes the swap harder to write, but only a wiring test makes it impossible to land. Those tests are also listed as item 3 of WB-01KY899X30206RKTM9XEBTZ4KA; do them once, here or there, and reference the other.

Acceptance:
- newHandler and the exported constructors take an options struct with named fields.
- The one production call site is updated and test call sites are migrated or given a small helper.
- Serve-level tests cover DELETE, restore, and history through real runServe wiring, and fail if the corresponding literals are swapped.
- Verify by actually swapping the delete and restore literals and confirming the suite goes red.
